with temporary.open('x') as stream:
    json.dump({'pid': pid, 'startTimeTicks': int(fields[19])}, stream)
os.replace(temporary, marker)

    json.dump({'pid': pid, 'startTimeTicks': int(fields[19])}, stream)
os.replace(temporary, marker)

os.replace(temporary, marker)

All raw command logs and full-tree manifests stay outside workspace trees but inside the measured Btrfs root.
Checkpoint sums CLI and authoritative readiness phases; its immediate raw acknowledgment ledger is outside those phases but inside full-task wall time.
Full-tree oracle checks types, ordinary modes, exact mtimes, file bytes, symlink targets and internal hardlink groups before any restored build.
Source and imported main are checked unchanged; main, work and restored second remain live at final physical accounting.
Writable checkpoint retains its old journal generation: four generations and three live views at final space.

A single ordinary compiler container is reused for foreground commands in one bound workspace generation; restored work uses a new container.
PID1 only waits for a unique marker in container-local /tmp, outside /work and the checkpoint oracle.

Unknown create/start/exec/exit/removal outcomes fail closed, retain evidence, block product unmount, and are never automatically retried or signaled.
Main/source read-only-purpose oracles use separately charged short-lived cooperative sessions; the source bind remains read-only.
transport_seconds is a diagnostic breakdown overlapping phase_seconds and full_task_seconds, never an amount to subtract from measured phases.

This is a separately labeled revised-transport series, not a direct speedup claim against the earlier per-command docker-run series.

The two convenience_seconds composites cover disjoint checkpoint and restore intervals but overlap their underlying phase/transport fields; never add both accounting layers. Restored compiler-start readiness is not full-tree verification.

Exactly17packages must compile on clean/edit and be Fresh on noop/restored; wrong or duplicate package observations fail.
Target hardlink/symlink/mode/exact-nanosecond-mtime probes and generated build artifacts stay in the full checkpoint oracle.

os.replace(temporary, marker)

measurementNotes: One immutable supplied image, fixed toolchain and --jobs 1; no image pull or build in this driver.

Cargo home, target, incremental caches and TMPDIR are within the actual /work tree; no target/cache cleanup or exclusion.
All raw command logs and full-tree manifests stay outside workspace trees but inside the measured Btrfs root.
Checkpoint sums CLI and authoritative readiness phases; its immediate raw acknowledgment ledger is outside those phases but inside full-task wall time.
Full-tree oracle checks types, ordinary modes, exact mtimes, file bytes, symlink targets and internal hardlink groups before any restored build.
Source and imported main are checked unchanged; main, work and restored second remain live at final physical accounting.
Writable checkpoint retains its old journal generation: four generations and three live views at final space.
Full-task wall time includes preparation, all oracles, command transport, physical accounting and final normal cleanup.
Whole-filesystem Used includes Data, Metadata and System, all store/runtime state and retained generations; parent owns runtime-ready baseline.
Cargo cache behavior comes from actual verbose outputs; restored paths do not imply a Fresh build or equal durability.
Harness never signals processes or uses force/lazy unmount; product-internal startup-failure behavior is not claimed absent.
A single ordinary compiler container is reused for foreground commands in one bound workspace generation; restored work uses a new container.
PID1 only waits for a unique marker in container-local /tmp, outside /work and the checkpoint oracle.

Before checkpoint and final product cleanup, marker exec is attempted once, its writer exits before PID1, natural PID1 exit is observed, docker wait confirms zero exit, then exact-container docker rm and absence checks complete.
Unknown create/start/exec/exit/removal outcomes fail closed, retain evidence, block product unmount, and are never automatically retried or signaled.
Main/source read-only-purpose oracles use separately charged short-lived cooperative sessions; the source bind remains read-only.
transport_seconds is a diagnostic breakdown overlapping phase_seconds and full_task_seconds, never an amount to subtract from measured phases.

os.replace(temporary, marker)

os.replace(temporary, marker)

measurementNotes: One immutable supplied image, fixed toolchain and --jobs 1; no image pull or build in this driver.
Default-root ordinary compiler containers have no added capabilities/devices or network/security flags.
Cargo home, target, incremental caches and TMPDIR are within the actual /work tree; no target/cache cleanup or exclusion.
All raw command logs and full-tree manifests stay outside workspace trees but inside the measured Btrfs root.
Checkpoint sums CLI and authoritative readiness phases; its immediate raw acknowledgment ledger is outside those phases but inside full-task wall time.
Full-tree oracle checks types, ordinary modes, exact mtimes, file bytes, symlink targets and internal hardlink groups before any restored build.
Source and imported main are checked unchanged; main, work and restored second remain live at final physical accounting.
Writable checkpoint retains its old journal generation: four generations and three live views at final space.
Full-task wall time includes preparation, all oracles, command transport, physical accounting and final normal cleanup.
Whole-filesystem Used includes Data, Metadata and System, all store/runtime state and retained generations; parent owns runtime-ready baseline.
Cargo cache behavior comes from actual verbose outputs; restored paths do not imply a Fresh build or equal durability.
Harness never signals processes or uses force/lazy unmount; product-internal startup-failure behavior is not claimed absent.
A single ordinary compiler container is reused for foreground commands in one bound workspace generation; restored work uses a new container.
PID1 only waits for a unique marker in container-local /tmp, outside /work and the checkpoint oracle.

Before checkpoint and final product cleanup, marker exec is attempted once, its writer exits before PID1, natural PID1 exit is observed, docker wait confirms zero exit, then exact-container docker rm and absence checks complete.
Unknown create/start/exec/exit/removal outcomes fail closed, retain evidence, block product unmount, and are never automatically retried or signaled.
Main/source read-only-purpose oracles use separately charged short-lived cooperative sessions; the source bind remains read-only.
transport_seconds is a diagnostic breakdown overlapping phase_seconds and full_task_seconds, never an amount to subtract from measured phases.
Session start is charged to its first command phase; pre-checkpoint stop and final cleanup have explicit phase fields. Full checkpoint CLI/readiness remains unchanged.

At active-space accounting exactly the restored-generation compiler container remains; its writable layer/logs plus Docker/containerd roots, image and product generations remain charged. Main/source transient sessions have already exited and been removed.
This is a separately labeled revised-transport series, not a direct speedup claim against the earlier per-command docker-run series.

The two convenience_seconds composites cover disjoint checkpoint and restore intervals but overlap their underlying phase/transport fields; never add both accounting layers. Restored compiler-start readiness is not full-tree verification.
New16-library+application local dependency DAG with real generated build-script output; frozen Cargo reports are not rewritten.
Exactly17packages must compile on clean/edit and be Fresh on noop/restored; wrong or duplicate package observations fail.
Target hardlink/symlink/mode/exact-nanosecond-mtime probes and generated build artifacts stay in the full checkpoint oracle.
All additional toolchain/probe/artifact verification runs are charged; complete logs copied only after space and normal cleanup.

os.replace(temporary, marker)

fields = pathlib.Path('/proc/self/stat').read_text().rpartition(') ')[2].split()

    json.dump({'pid': pid, 'startTimeTicks': int(fields[19])}, stream)
os.replace(temporary, marker)

A single ordinary compiler container is reused for foreground commands in one bound workspace generation; restored work uses a new container.
PID1 only waits for a unique marker in container-local /tmp, outside /work and the checkpoint oracle.

Before checkpoint and final product cleanup, marker exec is attempted once, its writer exits before PID1, natural PID1 exit is observed, docker wait confirms zero exit, then exact-container docker rm and absence checks complete.
Unknown create/start/exec/exit/removal outcomes fail closed, retain evidence, block product unmount, and are never automatically retried or signaled.

transport_seconds is a diagnostic breakdown overlapping phase_seconds and full_task_seconds, never an amount to subtract from measured phases.

os.replace(temporary, marker)

PID1 only waits for a unique marker in container-local /tmp, outside /work and the checkpoint oracle.

os.replace(temporary, marker)

measurementNotes: One immutable supplied image, fixed toolchain and --jobs 1; no image pull or build in this driver.
Default-root ordinary compiler containers have no added capabilities/devices or network/security flags.
Cargo home, target, incremental caches and TMPDIR are within the actual /work tree; no target/cache cleanup or exclusion.
All raw command logs and full-tree manifests stay outside workspace trees but inside the measured Btrfs root.
Checkpoint sums CLI and authoritative readiness phases; its immediate raw acknowledgment ledger is outside those phases but inside full-task wall time.
Full-tree oracle checks types, ordinary modes, exact mtimes, file bytes, symlink targets and internal hardlink groups before any restored build.
Source and imported main are checked unchanged; main, work and restored second remain live at final physical accounting.
Writable checkpoint retains its old journal generation: four generations and three live views at final space.
Full-task wall time includes preparation, all oracles, command transport, physical accounting and final normal cleanup.
Whole-filesystem Used includes Data, Metadata and System, all store/runtime state and retained generations; parent owns runtime-ready baseline.
Cargo cache behavior comes from actual verbose outputs; restored paths do not imply a Fresh build or equal durability.
Harness never signals processes or uses force/lazy unmount; product-internal startup-failure behavior is not claimed absent.
A single ordinary compiler container is reused for foreground commands in one bound workspace generation; restored work uses a new container.
PID1 only waits for a unique marker in container-local /tmp, outside /work and the checkpoint oracle.

Before checkpoint and final product cleanup, marker exec is attempted once, its writer exits before PID1, natural PID1 exit is observed, docker wait confirms zero exit, then exact-container docker rm and absence checks complete.
Unknown create/start/exec/exit/removal outcomes fail closed, retain evidence, block product unmount, and are never automatically retried or signaled.
Main/source read-only-purpose oracles use separately charged short-lived cooperative sessions; the source bind remains read-only.
transport_seconds is a diagnostic breakdown overlapping phase_seconds and full_task_seconds, never an amount to subtract from measured phases.
Session start is charged to its first command phase; pre-checkpoint stop and final cleanup have explicit phase fields. Full checkpoint CLI/readiness remains unchanged.

At active-space accounting exactly the restored-generation compiler container remains; its writable layer/logs plus Docker/containerd roots, image and product generations remain charged. Main/source transient sessions have already exited and been removed.
This is a separately labeled revised-transport series, not a direct speedup claim against the earlier per-command docker-run series.

The two convenience_seconds composites cover disjoint checkpoint and restore intervals but overlap their underlying phase/transport fields; never add both accounting layers. Restored compiler-start readiness is not full-tree verification.
New16-library+application local dependency DAG with real generated build-script output; frozen Cargo reports are not rewritten.
Exactly17packages must compile on clean/edit and be Fresh on noop/restored; wrong or duplicate package observations fail.
Target hardlink/symlink/mode/exact-nanosecond-mtime probes and generated build artifacts stay in the full checkpoint oracle.
All additional toolchain/probe/artifact verification runs are charged; complete logs copied only after space and normal cleanup.

import json, os, pathlib, sys
marker = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
pid = os.getpid()
fields = pathlib.Path('/proc/self/stat').read_text().rpartition(') ')[2].split()
temporary = marker.with_name(marker.name + '.' + str(pid))
with temporary.open('x') as stream:
    json.dump({'pid': pid, 'startTimeTicks': int(fields[19])}, stream)
os.replace(temporary, marker)
